claim: CoLLM-NAS, a two-stage LLM-guided NAS system using a stateful Navigator LLM plus stateless Generator LLM, surpasses existing NAS methods and conventional search algorithms on ImageNet and NAS-Bench-201 while cutting search cost 4-10x.
stance_target: Blanket claim that iterative LLM feedback degrades LLM-guided NAS proposals
scope_conditions: NAS-Bench-201 and ImageNet; MobileNet/ShuffleNet/AutoFormer search spaces; two-stage NAS pipelines (OFA, SPOS, AutoFormer)
quoted_support: CoLLM-NAS efficiently guides the search process by combining LLMs' inherent knowledge of structured neural architectures with progressive knowledge from iterative feedback and historical trajectory... achieving new state-of-the-art results while significantly reducing search costs by 4--10x.

claim: CoLLM-NAS uses a stateful Navigator LLM specifically to guide search direction using historical trajectory, i.e., a persistent multi-turn feedback loop rather than single-context sequential generation.
stance_target: Whether the target paper's negative feedback result generalizes across LLM-NAS architectures
quoted_support: we propose a stateful Navigator LLM to guide search direction, a stateless Generator LLM to synthesize high-quality candidates, and a Coordinator module to orchestrate inter-LLM communication and manage evaluation processes.

claim: Most existing LLM+NAS methods (as of 2025) face critical limitations including architectural invalidity, computational inefficiency, and inferior performance compared to traditional NAS.
stance_target: That prior LLM-NAS baselines already underperform, setting up a plausible field-wide skepticism the target paper's negative result fits into
scope_conditions: LLM-NAS literature as characterized by CoLLM-NAS authors, 2025
quoted_support: most existing methods face critical limitations, including architectural invalidity, computational inefficiency, and inferior performance compared to traditional NAS.

claim: CoLLM-NAS was accepted as an Oral at the CVPR 2026 Workshop on Neural Architecture Search, indicating an active, competing NAS-workshop venue outside NeurIPS that already features LLM-NAS work with positive iterative-feedback results.
